subject: Emb -> Reranker transition: migration roadmap and index backfill playbook
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mills <sara@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Emb -> Reranker transition: migration roadmap and index backfill playbook

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m opening this thread to drive the handoff and lay out a concrete, low-risk plan to move Nimbus’ existing embeddings into the reranker-backed search stack. Goal: keep search quality stable (or improve), limit user-facing regressions, and avoid a big migration window.

High-level approach (summary):
- Phase 0: Canary — run a 10k-document canary to validate vectorization + rerank scoring parity.
- Phase 1: Streaming backfill for recent / hot docs + incremental sync.
- Phase 2: Bulk historical backfill (batched, idempotent) off-hours with progress checkpoints.
- Phase 3: Cutover, fallback + rollback window, post-cutover validation.

What we need from Nimbus for the kickoff:
1) A sample manifest with doc IDs and canonical text (attached).
2) Credentials for the read-only snapshot of the content store (S3 or GCS) and test vector DB access (or a staging DB).
3) Confirmation on preferred vectorstore (you mentioned Pinecone and Milvus) and whether we can provision a staging namespace for the canary.

Technical notes (quick):
- ID mapping: we’ll keep your canonical doc_id as the primary key in the vectorstore and write idempotent upserts using the doc_id + source_version hash.
- Backfill throughput: expect ~250–500 docs/sec per worker for text->embedding + upsert depending on average doc length and vector DB choice; planning will include parallel workers and bulk write sizing.
- Rerank evals: we’ll run nDCG@10 and MRR@5 on the canary and a small query log sample; we’ll also measure recall lift on judged queries you provide.

I’ve attached a small manifest (nimbus_embedding_manifest.csv) and a seed set of canary queries (canary_eval_queries.json). Please confirm who on your side will own the snapshot access and whether we should open a short VPC peering/egress rule for the staging phase.

Proposed next step: 30-minute kickoff Friday 2027-05-21 10:00 PT to align SOCs, access, and assign JIRA tasks — does that work for you?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Emb -> Reranker transition: migration roadmap and index backfill playbook

Alex —

This looks good, thank you. Quick clarifications:
- We prefer Milvus for our long-term index but can stand up a Pinecone staging namespace if that makes the canary faster to run.
- We can provide an S3 snapshot URL + IAM role for read-only access. I’ll send that to ops with the bucket path.
- Do you expect the canary to impact production traffic? We want no search regressions during weekdays.

I’m looping in our ops alias to coordinate the S3 creds. Friday 10:00 PT works for our team.

—Sara
Head of Search, Nimbus Analytics
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mills <sara@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emb -> Reranker transition: migration roadmap and index backfill playbook

Sara — great, thanks for the fast reply. Short answers:
- Milvus is fine for production; for the canary we prefer a lightweight staging namespace to avoid quota interactions. We’ll recommend a Pinecone staging if you can spin it up quickly — we have a ready connector for both.
- Canary impact: zero production traffic change if we run queries against a shadow stack and compare scores; the only risk is sampling bias. For production-side switching we’ll do a 30-minute maintenance window with immediate rollback if we observe regressions.

Details for Friday kickoff:
- Deliverables we’ll produce in the first 72 hours: canary evaluation report (nDCG, MRR), a runbook for the bulk backfill, and a mutual action plan with responsibilities.
- Backfill mechanics: recommended pattern is incremental streaming of latest X days (configurable) + staged bulk for older content. Bulk backfill will be done via compressed NDJSON batches, with final consistency verification (hash check) after each shard.
- Cost/throughput tradeoffs: Milvus managed on your cloud will be cheaper per-write but higher maintenance; Pinecone has faster bulk ingest at small scale. We’ll provide an estimated token and compute cost profile once we see the manifest sample sizes.

Operational asks for your ops team (put on Friday agenda):
1) Create a read-only IAM role for the S3 bucket or provide an S3 pre-signed URL list.
2) Provision a staging vectorstore namespace (Pinecone or Milvus).
3) Share a representative query log slice (anonymized) for rerank evals.

I’ll upload a draft mutual action plan and a tentative backfill calendar ahead of the call (link in thread).

—Alex
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Sara Mills <sara@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emb -> Reranker transition: migration roadmap and index backfill playbook

Hi Sara / Alex —

I’ll run the kickoff and take point on the mutual action plan. A few operational details I’ll cover on the call:
- JIRA: I’ve opened NIM-IMPL-432 with the first three epics (canary, streaming sync, bulk backfill). I’ll add owners and acceptance criteria during the meeting.
- Security: we’ll need to confirm KMS key access if you plan to ship encrypted snapshots; also SOC 2 evidence for the staging environment if you want Red-team scans.
- Metrics: please confirm the primary success metrics you want in the canary report (I’d recommend nDCG@10, MRR@5, query latency P95).

On timelines — tentative plan: canary week of 2027-05-24, streaming sync starting 2027-05-31, bulk backfill week of 2027-06-14 (off-hours windows). We’ll aim for a gradual cutover the week after backfill completes with a 72-hour observation period and automated rollback hooks.

Attachments: I uploaded a starter mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) to the Drive link in my calendar invite.

Thanks — Monica
